rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The denial and its coordinated clauses answer the preceding oath.
rows.anchor: bu ve ma‘tufları kasemin cevâbıdır

rows.speaker: Ebû Hayyân
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan takes bi as an oath particle in a parenthetical clause, strengthening the negation.
rows.anchor: Ebû Hayyân nefiyde daha ziyade kuvvet ifade etmek üzere cümle-i mu‘teriza hâlinde kasem için olmasını zâhir görmüştür

rows.speaker: İbn Atıyye
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya treats the phrase as a parenthetical like bihamdillah: by God's praise, you possess virtue.
rows.anchor: bi-hamdillah sâhib-i faziletsin

rows.speaker: Zemahşerî
rows.claim: Zamakhshari attaches bi to the negated predicate: by God's favor the Prophet is rational, with that favor underlying both the denial of madness and affirmation of reason.
rows.anchor: Zemahşerî ise menfî olan habere ta‘allukuyla

rows.speaker: Zemahşerî
rows.claim: Alternatively, Zamakhshari construes the phrase as a stable adverbial state from anta.
rows.anchor: zarf-ı müstekar olarak أَنتَ’den hâl olmasını söylemiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's favor means prophethood and its prerequisites: intellect, discernment, good character, virtue, and gifts that bring worldly and afterlife felicity.
rows.anchor: nübüvvet ve levâzımı olan akıl ve şehâmet ve hüsn-i ahlâk

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the start of revelation, Meccan opponents out of envy, hostility, and confusion falsely accused Muhammad of madness and error; he is instead distinguished by reason, uprightness, and virtue bestowed by God for his mission.
rows.anchor: Mekke küffârının hased ve adavet ve şaşkınlıkla nisbet etmeye kalkıştıkları mecnunluk ve sapıklık şâibelerinin kendisinden uzak, bilakis onun akl ü şehâmet

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghayr mamnun means uninterrupted, inexhaustible reward, or reward consisting solely of God's generosity without anyone else's favor.
rows.anchor: yahut hiç kimsenin minnetini çekmeksizin mahza Allah’ın lutf ü inayeti

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God promises the Prophet endless, obligation-free reward and gifts in return for the harms and hardships he will face.
rows.anchor: ileride minnetsiz ve tükenmez ecr ü nimetlere nâil olmak üzere bulunduğunu beyan ve vaad

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet was created with very great dispositions, virtues, and spiritual qualities that lead through action toward the highest good; he will attain that goal by following them.
rows.anchor: pek büyük huylar, hakikaten tazime lâyık seciye ve meleke ve mâneviyat üzere yaratılmış bulunuyorsun. Onunla yürüyecek o gayeye ereceksin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This great character is the straight path and true religion of Islam, formed by Qur'anic etiquette and divine ethics bestowed by God; the Prophet is the believers' good example.
rows.anchor: İşte o ahlâk sırât-ı müstakīmi, dîn-i hak olan dîn-i İslâm’ı teşkil eden

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People fail to grasp the greatness of this character and commit follies that require patience and endurance.
rows.anchor: Onun büyüklüğünü halk idrak edemez de sabr u tahammül edilmesi iktizâ eden deliliklerde bulunurlar

rows.speaker: Râgıb
rows.claim: Al-Raghib says khalq and khuluq share an origin like sharb/shurb and sarm/surm; with fatḥ khalq is the visible form, while with ḍamm khuluq is a faculty perceived by the heart.
rows.anchor: “halk” ve “hulk” aslında birdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khuluq has plurals huluk and akhlaq; in Turkish akhlaq is commonly used as a singular, like evlad.
rows.anchor: Fakat lisânımızda “ahlâk” kelimesinin de “evlâd” kelimesi gibi müfred makamında

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Character denotes settled dispositions; depending on whether one habitually follows good or evil, one distinguishes praiseworthy and blameworthy character.
rows.anchor: meleke ve rüsuh esas olduğundan hayır veya şerri itiyad etmiş olmasına nazaran ahlâk-ı hasene ve ahlâk-ı seyyie

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the phrase as a great religion, specifically Islam.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas’tan: 1. Azîm bir din, 2. Azîm bir din ki o İslâm’dır

rows.speaker: Mücâhid
rows.claim: Mujahid explains the Prophet's great character as religion.
rows.anchor: Mücâhid’den: Din. İbn Zeyd’den; edeb-i Kur’an

rows.speaker: İbn Zeyd
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd identifies the Prophet's character as Qur'anic etiquette.
rows.anchor: Mücâhid’den: Din. İbn Zeyd’den; edeb-i Kur’an

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Sa'id b. Hisham reports asking Aisha about the Prophet's character; she answered that his character was the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: Resûlullah’ın ahlâkını Hazret-i Âişe’den sordum

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One sense of Aisha's answer is that the Prophet embodied all the Qur'an's noble qualities and was protected from its condemned defects, fully exemplifying Hud 11:112.
rows.anchor: Kur’an’daki büyük mekârim-i ahlâkın hepsi onda vardı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Understanding this first sense fully requires understanding the Qur'an in its entirety.
rows.anchor: Onu anlamak Kur’ân’ı tamamen anlamaya mütevakkıftır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second sense is that the Prophet's character was so great that no other description could adequately express it.
rows.anchor: öyle büyük bir ahlâk idi ki onu başka bir târif ile anlatmak kābil değildir demek olur

rows.speaker: ضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says this is the religion and command God ordered the Prophet and entrusted him to uphold.
rows.anchor: Dahhâk’tan لَعَلَىٰ خُلُقٍ عَظِيمٍۢ yani Allah’ın ona emrettiği ve onu müvekkel kıldığı dini ve emri

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tanwin of khuluq magnifies the quality: the Prophet's character has beauties others cannot fully comprehend.
rows.anchor: Burada خُلُقٍ’daki tenvin tefhıym içindir ki sâirlerinin hakkıyla idrak edemeyecekleri güzelliklerle mümtaz bir ahlâk demektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic inna, initial lām, magnifying tanwin, and adjective azim multiply assurances of the Prophet's lofty character; the clause also reinforces the preceding oath response.
rows.anchor: azamet ü ulviyeti kat kat te’mînât içinde beyan ve tebliğ buyurulmuş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı presents the verse as a distinguished great sign among the lines written by the Supreme Pen in the clear Book.
rows.anchor: bu Kitâb-ı Mübîn’de Kalem-i A‘lâ’nın yazdığı satırların azîm bir âyet-i mümtâzesi olmak üzere konulmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's character will become visible in future action, even to his enemies, strengthening him and the believers while warning those who accuse him of madness.
rows.anchor: ileride kuvveden fiile çıkarak tecribe sahasındaki tecelliyâtıyla düşmanlar nazarında dahi görüleceğini vaad

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Meftun can mean someone afflicted by trial and madness as a passive participle, or fitna and madness as a verbal noun.
rows.anchor: fitne ve belâya tutulmuş mecnun demek olduğu gibi masdar olarak fitne ve cünun mânasına da gelir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prefixed bi leads exegetes to prefer the verbal-noun sense: which side has the madness, the Prophet or his pagan accusers; the passive-participle reading asks which side is afflicted, and both are valid.
rows.anchor: buyurulmuş olduğu cihetle müfessirîn ikinci mânayı daha müreccah görmüşlerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the passive-participle reading, the question asks whether the Prophet or those pagans calling him mad are afflicted; on the verbal-noun reading, it asks which side has madness.
rows.anchor: iki mâna da doğrudur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad is told to ask which opponent would guarantee such an irrational judgment, unsupported by reason or revelation, or who had obtained God's undertaking for it.
rows.anchor: içlerinden hangisi imiş ona za‘îm aklî naklî hiçbir delilin, hiçbir akl u iz‘ânın kabul edemeyeceği öyle bir hükmün doğruluğuna içlerinden kefil

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alleged partners may be imitators who follow their desires or the idols the opponents follow, supposedly empowering them to alter truth and make God treat Muslims as criminals.
rows.anchor: Onlara o hükümde iştirak eden, gönüllerinin istediğine taklid suretiyle

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If they are truthful, let them bring their partners; no force can alter God's judgment or change truth, and all are humbled before it.
rows.anchor: dünya bir tarafa gelse Allah’ın bir hükmünü tebdil edemez, bir hakikati değiştiremez, hepsi hakkın karşısında zelîl ü makhur olmaya mahkumdurlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saq literally means the shin from ankle toward calf, and by extension the basis or trunk of something; here it is indefinite and not annexed to anything.
rows.anchor: lügatta mâlum ki topuktan baldıra doğru bacağın incik yeridir

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد
rows.claim: Abu Sa'id reports the Prophet: when the Lord unveils His shin, believers prostrate; those who prostrated ostentatiously in worldly life try, but their backs stiffen into one piece.
rows.anchor: Buhârî, Müslim, Nesâî, İbn Münzir ve İbn Merdûye, Ebû Sa‘îd radıyallahu anh’tan şöyle bir hadîs rivayet etmişlerdir

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Mas'ud reports the Prophet: after each person is sent to follow the worldly deity they worshipped, Muslims recognize their Lord by the unveiling of the shin and prostrate, while hypocrites cannot bend their backs.
rows.anchor: İbn Mes‘ûd’dan, Hazret-i Peygamber sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem’den bir hadis rivayet etmişlerdir

rows.speaker: Dârekutnî ve Hâkim
rows.claim: Al-Daraqutni and al-Hakim grade the Ibn Mas'ud narration sound.
rows.anchor: Dârekutnî ve Hâkim sahih diye

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hadiths are ambiguous reports whose modality God will reveal in events at their appointed time; the unveiling signifies truth appearing from the unseen with terrible force, bringing mercy to truth's adherents and wrath to falsehood's.
rows.anchor: hadislerde keyfiyeti ihâta olunamayacak müteşabih bir mâna vardır ki Allah teâlâ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The image is a divine sign of truth's manifestation that strips people's veils of heedlessness and displays God's judgment; its actual manner cannot now be specified.
rows.anchor: insanlardan gaflet perdelerini sıyıracak bir şiddet ve dehşetle hükm-i Hakk’ın ehl-i Hakk’a rahmet

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı says the verse contains a symbolic sign like the letter nun.
rows.anchor: Bu itibar ile burada da ن gibi bir remiz vardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some seekers of ambiguous texts corporealize God against 42:11, while certain esoteric Sufis likewise insist on a literal visual manifestation; Elmalılı rejects such literalizing approaches.
rows.anchor: koşan birtakım kimseler bunlardan tecsim ve teşbih

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: The Kashshaf glosses uncovering the shin and baring calves as idioms for an affair's severity and calamity's difficulty, originating in people fleeing in terror with garments raised.
rows.anchor: tâbirleri emrin şiddetinde ve musibetin su‘ûbetinde meseldir

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says obscure Qur'anic language should be investigated in poetry, the Arabs' register; the quoted line interprets the image as war at full severity.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas’tan bu âyetin tefsîri sorulduğunda demiştir ki

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the saq as hardship and severity, citing an Arabic verse about war standing on a shin.
rows.anchor: O kerb ü şiddet günüdür.

rows.speaker: مجاهِد
rows.claim: Mujahid says this is the most severe hour of the Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: Mücâhid de ondan bugün kıyametin en şiddetli saati olduğunu rivayet eylemiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited Arabic poetry establishes that saq can figuratively mean severity; since definitive proofs rule out assigning a literal shin to God, the figurative sense is necessary.
rows.anchor: Allah teâlâ’ya hakikat mânasıyla sâk isnâdı delâil-i kat‘iyye ile muhâl olduğundan mecaz ta‘ayyün eder

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الضرير
rows.claim: Al-Razi reports Abu Sa'id al-Darir's view that saq is a thing's sustaining basis; unveiling it means the affair's core and the realities of things will emerge on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: İkinci kavil, Ebû Sa‘îd-i Darîr’in

rows.speaker: Fahr-ı Râzî
rows.claim: Al-Razi records a third proposal: the shin belongs to Hell, the Throne, or a majestic angel, though the verse names no possessor.
rows.anchor: Üçüncü kavil, Cehennemin sâkı yahut Arş’ın sâkı yahut mehîb bir meleğin sâkı demektir

rows.speaker: Müşebbihe
rows.claim: Al-Razi reports that the Mushabbiha identify it as God's shin, but rejects corporeal attribution and reading related Ibn Mas'ud reports bodily; the verse's noun is indefinite.
rows.anchor: Dördüncü kavil, Müşebbihe’nin ihtiyârıdır ki Allah’ın sâkı demişlerdir.

rows.speaker: حاتم
rows.claim: Hatem's line depicts reciprocal biting in war and war baring its calves, illustrating the idiom of extreme hardship.
rows.anchor: Hâtim demiştir ki: أَخُو الْحَرْبِ

rows.speaker: ابن رقيات
rows.claim: Ibn Rukayyat's poem says terror distracts an elder from his sons and makes a sheltered, modest young woman expose her calves, supporting the severity idiom.
rows.anchor: İbn Rukayyat da şöyle demiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means God's command grows severe and the affair intensifies, not that a shin literally exists or is uncovered; describing a miser as hand-bound similarly conveys miserliness without a literal hand or bond.
rows.anchor: Yoksa ne sâk vardır ne de keşif

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı rejects the corporeal reading of the Ibn Mas'ud hadith, explaining it as the intensification of God's command and the Great Terror of 21:103.
rows.anchor: demektir ki o kıyamet günü

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority identifies this day as the Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: Birincisi, cumhûrun kavli: bugün kıyamet günüdür

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abu Muslim says the day is in worldly life, since the verse describes people being called to prostrate and there is no worship or legal obligation at Resurrection.
rows.anchor: İkincisi de Ebû Müslim’in kavlidir ki bugün kıyamet günü değil, dünyadadır.

words: وَقَدْ كَانُوا۟ يُدْعَوْنَ إِلَى ٱلسُّجُودِ وَهُمْ سَٰلِمُونَ
rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abu Muslim proposes either a person's last day, when angels appear without glad tidings and a late conversion no longer helps, or an illness, old age, or incapacity that prevents prostration despite earlier soundness.
rows.anchor: Ebû Müslim’in kavlidir ki bugün kıyamet günü değil, dünyadadır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı allows Abu Muslim's worldly reading but rejects his claim that Resurrection is impossible: the call there is reproach and condemnation, not a legal command; their imposed inability increases regret for neglecting prostration while sound.
rows.anchor: âyetin lafzını Ebû Müslim’in dediğine haml mümkin

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan explains unveiling the shin as an idiom for affairs becoming severe; his citation treats the metaphor as common in Arabic.
rows.anchor: ‘Keşf-i sâk’ emrin şiddetinden ve gittikçe büyümesinden kinayedir

rows.speaker: مجاهِد
rows.claim: Mujahid identifies the severity as the most dreadful first hour of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: Mücâhid şöyle demiştir: Bu şiddet kıyametin ilk saatidir ve en fecî‘idir

rows.speaker: راجز
rows.claim: An anonymous rajiz describes a red drought year as exposing its shin and stripping meat from bones, another example of the severity idiom.
rows.anchor: beytinden başka râciz demiştir ki: عَجِبْتُ مِنْ نَفْسِي

rows.speaker: راجز
rows.claim: Another rajiz says war has bared its calves and grown serious, so the fighters must buckle down.
rows.anchor: Diğer bir râciz: قَدْ شَ َّمرَتْ عَنْ سَاقِهَا

rows.speaker: راجز
rows.claim: A further rajiz uses the idiom that war stands on a shin, exhorting steadfastness amid battle.
rows.anchor: Bir diğeri: صبرا امام آن شر ب اق

rows.speaker: شاعر
rows.claim: An unnamed poet says war revealed its shin and ruin appeared, extending the same hardship imagery.
rows.anchor: Bir şâ‘ir de demiştir ki

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the phrase as a day when a severe ordeal is uncovered.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas demiştir ki: يـَوْمَ يُكْشَفُ عَنْ شِ َّدةٍ

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda says saq is used for severity and kashafa an saqihi means gathering up one's garment; Arabs call a drought year one that has bared its shin.
rows.anchor: Bundan dolayı Arab kıtlık senesine

rows.speaker: Zemahşerî
rows.claim: Zamakhshari says the indefinite saq points to an unfamiliar, extreme ordeal, like the unknown calamity named in 54:6.
rows.anchor: Zemahşerî’nin dediği gibi şiddette me’luftan hâriç bir emr-i mübheme
